# /run-pipeline — eBay Car Part Pipeline

Sequential delegation: Agent 1 → Agent 2 → Agent 3.

**Do not edit this file, and do not edit any configuration.** You are the coordinator: you delegate,
you write the two intermediate result files in `./output/`, and as the last step you run one
conversion script (step 9). Nothing else. On previous runs a coordinator overwrote this file with a
three-line stub and destroyed every guardrail below, and another edited `.pi/settings.json` trying
to fix a model error mid-run. Both made things worse.

Specifically, never touch: this file, `.pi/settings.json`, `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, anything in
`.pi/agents/`, or `.pi/extensions/`. If a run fails, **stop and report the error verbatim** — do not
diagnose it, do not edit config to work around it, do not retry with altered settings. Configuration
here is deliberate and was arrived at painfully; a plausible-looking fix will undo work you cannot
see.

## Launching pi for this job

```
cd "/Users/tamaugo/Desktop/ebay-pipeline/harness"
pi
```

No flags. **Do NOT pass `-ne`** — it disables extension discovery and would strip the `subagent`
tool this orchestration depends on. Older notes say to launch with `-ne -e ...`; that advice is
obsolete as of 2026-09-04 and now actively wrong.

The tool-name collision it worked around (the global `pi-interactive-subagents` and the project-local
`@baryonlabs/pi-agent-harness` both register `subagent`) is now fixed properly in `.pi/settings.json`,
which force-unloads the global package's extension for this project only. If that entry is ever lost,
nothing here will run. `.pi/settings.json` also caps `meta/muse-spark-1.3` at 16,384 max output
tokens — without that cap OpenRouter rejects every Agent 2 and Agent 3 call with a 402, because pi
otherwise requests the model's advertised 943,718-token ceiling, which exceeds the API key's budget.

**Do NOT pass `--tools`** on a pipeline run — it is a strict allowlist and would disable the built-in
read/write tools this orchestration needs. `EBAY_APP_ID` and `EBAY_CERT_ID` must be set in the shell
*before* launching pi; child agents inherit pi's environment.

## Delegation settings — use these on EVERY subagent call

```
agentScope: "both"
confirmProjectAgents: false
```

`agentScope` defaults to `"user"`, but all three agents are project-local, so omitting it makes the
call fail and wastes turns rediscovering why. `confirmProjectAgents` defaults to `true`, which stops
and asks the operator before every agent — unnecessary here.

### How to delegate — one mode per call, everything inside `task`

The `subagent` tool takes **exactly one mode** per call (`agent`+`task`, or `tasks`, or `chain`); any
other combination fails with `Invalid parameters. Provide exactly one mode.` Use **single mode, one
call per step**, so you can write files and count lines between steps. There is no parameter for
photos, vehicle strings or file contents: the agent sees only the `task` string, so put every path
and every file's text in it. Never pass `tasks` or `chain`, and never add fields like `photos`.

```
subagent({ agent: "<agent name>", task: "<full text the agent needs>",
           agentScope: "both", confirmProjectAgents: false })
```

- **Step 1** — `task`: the car make, then the part-photo paths one per line, each quoted, exactly as
  listed (`"photos/IMG 0118.JPEG"`). NULL photos are never included.
- **Step 4** — `task`: the full verbatim contents of `agent1_results.md`, nothing added or trimmed.
- **Step 7** — `task`: the full verbatim contents of `agent2_results.md`; then a line
  `Vehicle string: <verbatim>`; then `NULL filenames: <one per line, or "none">`; then
  `Write output to: <output>/agent3_results.txt`.

If a `subagent` call is rejected with a parameter error twice in a row, **stop and report the error
verbatim** — do not compose a third attempt from the same guess. The call template above is the
correct shape; any rejection after two tries means something else is wrong, and silent looping on
parameter errors has stalled a previous run entirely.

## Keep coordination cheap

On a previous run the coordinator cost $0.059 while the agent it was coordinating cost $0.0043 —
fourteen times the price of the actual work, almost all of it avoidable exploration.

- **Do not rediscover configuration.** Everything about the setup is stated here. Do not `ls` the
  agents directory, do not `grep` agent frontmatter, do not inspect `.pi/`.
- **But DO look at the input data.** Listing the photo folder and the output folder is required
  work, not exploration. The rule above is about configuration you have already been told; it never
  applies to the images you are being asked to process. A previous run read it too broadly, never
  listed `photos/`, guessed at a filename pattern, matched nothing, and reported an empty folder
  that held four images. **Never conclude a folder is empty without listing it.**
- The three agents are `agent1-part-reader`, `agent2-ebay-lookup`, `agent3-compiler`. They exist,
  they are project-local, they are configured correctly. Take that as given.
- `./photos` holds the images. `./output` is the output folder.
- Delegate, write the file, move on. Do not re-read a file you just wrote, do not summarise
  intermediate results to yourself, and do not verify an agent's work beyond the counts asked for.
  Checking that a file exists and counting its lines is not re-reading it — those checks are asked
  for in the steps below and are cheap; opening a file to admire or re-summarise it is not.

## Finding the photos — read this before listing anything

Image files in this project are usually **uppercase `.JPEG`**, and filenames **may contain spaces**.
Both have caused a run to fail by reporting an empty folder that was not empty.

- **Never glob for lowercase extensions.** `photos/*.jpg` and `photos/*.jpeg` match nothing here even
  though the files exist, because globbing is case-sensitive regardless of the filesystem.
- **List the directory itself** (`ls photos/`) rather than globbing by extension, and ignore
  `.DS_Store`.
- **Always quote paths.** `"photos/0118 part number.JPEG"`, never `photos/0118 part number.JPEG`.
- If a folder looks empty, **say what command you ran and stop** — do not conclude it is empty. It
  has been wrong every time so far.
- **A code before the extension is normal and expected.** Filenames may end `NSF`, `NSR`, `OSF`,
  `OSR` (near/off side, front/rear) or `NULL`, separated by an underscore **or a hyphen** — both are
  used: `img_2225_OSF.JPEG`, `IMG-NSF.JPEG`, `IMG4-NSF-NULL.JPEG`. That is the operator recording
  where on the car the part came from, and whether it has a part number at all. Agent 3 reads the
  location codes itself; you do nothing with those. Do not treat a code as an anomaly, do not strip
  or rewrite it, and **never rename a file** — pass filenames through exactly as they are so every
  stage can be traced back to its photo.
- **`NULL` is the one code you DO act on. See step 0 below.**
- **One photo = one part. Every photo carries a visible part number, EXCEPT the `NULL` ones.** The operator prepares the
  job that way, so the expected shape of a run is one line per image at every stage. This is a
  property of the input, not something you police: if Agent 1 still cannot read a number, its
  failure line *is* the correct output and travels down the chain untouched. Never re-crop, re-send,
  re-run or skip an image to improve the numbers.

## Inputs (ask the user if not already given)

- **Vehicle string** (required) — the operator's own description of the car, given at job start,
  e.g. `MAZDA 6 MK2 2008 SEDAN 2.5 PETROL`. Agent 3 writes it into every success row, so it reaches
  the customer. **Pass it on verbatim**: same words, same order, same capitalisation, nothing added
  or dropped. Never invent one, never expand or abbreviate it, never "correct" it, and never derive
  one from the part numbers or from eBay listing titles — a listing title describes the car the
  *seller* had, which is frequently not this car, and a coordinator's guess at trim or engine size
  is indistinguishable from fact once it is in the spreadsheet. If the operator has not given you a
  vehicle string, ask for it and wait.
- Car make and year (required — Agent 1 needs it for its format sanity check). Usually the opening
  words of the vehicle string, but ask rather than assume if the string is unusual.
- Photo folder (default `./photos`), output folder (default `./output`)

Pipeline rule: one folder = one make/year. Confirm both before running against unfamiliar data.

## Steps

0. **Split the folder first.** List the photo folder and separate it into two groups by filename:
   split each filename on underscores, hyphens and spaces, and if **any** token is exactly `NULL`
   (case-insensitive) it is a **NULL photo**; everything else is a **part photo**. Scan every token,
   not just the last — `IMG6-OUT-DOOR-HANDLE NSF-NULL.JPEG` is a NULL photo. A token must match
   exactly: `NULLJPEG` is a typing slip, not a code, and is treated as a normal part photo.

   NULL means the operator already knows that part has no number printed on it anywhere. He
   photographs it and files it with the rest on purpose, so there is only ever one folder to work
   through. Sending it to Agent 1 would spend a vision call to be told what he already told you, and
   risks Agent 1 inventing a number off a casting mark. So these are held back here — no vision
   call, no eBay search — and handed straight to Agent 3 at step 7.

   Report both counts before going further. If EVERY photo is NULL there is nothing for Agents 1 and
   2 to do: skip to step 7 with an empty Agent 2 result set and the full NULL list.

1. Delegate to `agent1-part-reader` with **the part photos only** — never a NULL photo — plus the
   stated car make.
2. Write its response verbatim to `<output>/agent1_results.md`. Do not edit, reformat or reorder it.
3. Confirm every **part photo** has a line — NULL photos are excluded and must not appear here. One
   photo is one part, and Agent 1's own rules say N images in → N result blocks out, so a mismatch is
   a real bug — surface it, never silently fix it.
4. Delegate to `agent2-ebay-lookup`, passing the full contents of `agent1_results.md`.
5. Write Agent 2's response verbatim to `<output>/agent2_results.md`.
6. Check the line count against step 3. **Count lines, not fields.** Agent 2's success lines now
   carry five fields (`filename | part_number | part name | price | url`) and its failure lines carry
   four; both are one line, and line-count parity is the only thing being checked here. A differing
   field count between a success line and a failure line is normal and is never something to
   "correct". Nor is the URL field itself: leave it exactly as Agent 2 wrote it, including a success
   line whose URL field is empty — that is a deliberate allowance for a listing that came back
   without a link, not a broken line. If a filename does appear on more than one line, leave every
   line as it is and mention it in the final report; never merge, delete or reorder lines to make
   counts tidy.
7. Delegate to `agent3-compiler`, passing four things: the contents of `agent2_results.md`, the
   **vehicle string verbatim**, the **list of NULL filenames** from step 0, and the output path
   `<output>/agent3_results.txt`. Agent 3 writes that file itself.

   Pass the NULL list explicitly **even when it is empty**, and say so — an absent list and a job
   with no NULL photos look identical to Agent 3, and it has no way to ask.
8. Confirm `agent3_results.txt` exists and its line count equals **step 6's count plus the number of
   NULL photos from step 0**. Agent 3 writes one row per Agent 2 line plus one row per NULL
   photo. **It also sorts every row by image number**, so its output is deliberately not in the
   order you handed it over — `IMG2` now comes before `IMG10`, and NULL rows sit among the others
   rather than in a block. That is correct and is not something to fix. Check the count, not the
   order. **Agent 3 no longer writes
   markdown.** It writes a pipe-delimited text file, four fields per line —
   `part info | price | url | image` — which is the input the converter in step 9 expects. Do not ask
   it for `.md`, and do not reformat, re-indent or bullet what it writes.

9. Run the output validator on Agent 3's file **before** converting it:

   ```
   python3 ../tools/agent3_validator.py <output>/agent3_results.txt <output>/agent2_results.md
   ```

   (Run it from the harness folder; the validator lives in the repo's `tools/` directory.) The
   validator deterministically checks every rule Agent 3 must follow and repairs what the rules
   define uniquely — row order, price format and floor, row remaps when a part number uniquely
   identifies its filename — marking anything that needs your judgment. Exit code `0` = clean or
   repaired, and the run continues. Exit code `2` = one or more rows are **marked** for
   investigation: report which rows and why, **stop there**, and do not convert to .xlsx until the
   operator says the marks are acceptable. A marked row reaching a customer is worse than a
   stopped run. Do not edit the validator, do not hand-edit the .txt to silence it.

10. Convert that text file into the spreadsheet the operator actually uses:

   ```
   python3 make_xlsx.py <output>/agent3_results.txt <output>/BEAR_results.xlsx
   ```

   Run it from the harness folder, where `make_xlsx.py` lives. This is the one command you run
   yourself — it is not configuration and not exploration, and the run is not finished without it,
   because the .txt file is an intermediate and the .xlsx is the deliverable. The script is
   deliberately dumb: it makes no judgement calls and every formatting rule lives in Agent 3's
   prompt. If it errors, **report the error verbatim and stop** — do not edit the script, do not
   hand-edit the .txt to get past a complaint, and do not build a spreadsheet by hand.
11. Confirm `<output>/BEAR_results.xlsx` exists.
12. Report briefly: images in, split into part photos and NULL photos; Agent 1 failures; Agent 2
    failures **split by type** (`No eBay Listing Found` vs `eBay Lookup Unavailable` — these mean
    different things and must be counted separately); Agent 3 malformed-line failures; whether the
    validator repaired anything or marked rows (and which); final line count; and that
    `<output>/BEAR_results.xlsx` was written.

    Count NULL photos separately from failures and never fold them together. A NULL row is the
    system working exactly as intended; a failure is something that went wrong. Reporting "5
    failures" when three of them were parts the operator already knew had no number would send him
    looking for a fault that is not there.

## Notes

- **Agent 2 is live-validated** (2026-09-03): it calls `ebay_search` itself and returns real UK
  listing data with its own tie-break applied. Active listings only — no sold-price source connected.
- **`getRateLimits` is a stub.** It always reports quota fine. Safe at test volume only.
- **Agent 3 is validated against fixtures** (15/15) but not yet against a live pipeline run.
- **`make_xlsx.py` is a deterministic converter, not an agent.** Agent 3 is a language model and
  cannot emit a .xlsx (it is a binary zip of XML); so it writes text and the script builds the
  workbook. A malformed row is written into the sheet with a `MALFORMED` marker rather than dropped,
  so a bad row is visible in the output — if you see one, report it, do not try to repair it.
- **Cost now scales ~linearly with batch size** (Jev fork, 2026-09-28): Agent 2 moved to
  mistral-nemo and Agent 3 to qwen3.8-flash, so the sequential-conversation quadratic term sits on
  ~$0.02-0.15/MTok models instead of $1.25/$4.25 — a 60-part job costs ~2.4p of LLM spend
  (`tools/cost_model_jev.py` has the full model). Chunking is no longer urgent.
  See `docs/pipeline-spec-jev.md` and `docs/Agent 2 Model & Cost Decision Record.docx`.
- To A/B an agent's model, edit the single `model:` line in its `.pi/agents/*.md`. Avoid
  `meta/muse-spark-1.2` with a thinking suffix — its reasoning endpoint is blocked by account policy.
